newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany votes to cut benefits for Bosnian refugees.
newsitem.headline: Germany votes to cut benefits for Bosnian refugees.

text.p: Germany's lower house of parliament on Thursday voted to cut social benefits by 20 percent for asylum seekers and Bosnian refugees and use the money saved to build homes in Bosnia.

The upper house of parliament is expected to approve the law on Friday, which means asylum seekers would receive 20 percent less social benefits than German nationals for three years rather than the one year under the current rule.
Bosnian refugees had previously been excluded from the rule which limited benefits for asylum seekers.

Germany's 16 regional states, which took in over 300,000 Bosnian refugees, will pay 750 million marks ($440 million) into a special fund over the next five years for the building and renovation of homes in Bosnia.

Several states have started forcibly repatriating Bosnian refugees, but critics have called on the state interior ministers not to rush as an influx of homeless returnees could aggravate the unstable situation in Bosnia.
A cross-party delegation of Bonn parliamentarians, which visited Bosnia this year, said many refugees had failed to find homes on their return to Bosnia. ($ = 1.716 German Marks)
